mainTopic: Pesachim 15b: The sources and time frame of the dispute between רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי about burning pure and impure תרומה together on ערב פסח.
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא in which בית שמאי and בית הלל argue whether פיגול, נותר and impure meat may be burned together. The גמרא then asks why רבי יוסי seems to answer רבי מאיר about רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים if רבי מאיר was quoting רבי יהושע. רב נחמן explains that the debate had two rounds, and that רבי יוסי first misunderstood which source רבי מאיר meant. רבי יהושע's barrel case is shown to be different because it prevents a large loss of חולין, and a small loss of firewood does not count. Then רבי יוחנן limits the whole dispute to the sixth hour, when חמץ is forbidden only by the חכמים. In the seventh hour everyone agrees that pure and impure תרומה are burned together. Two proofs for this, from פיגול and from moldy bread, are each rejected. Finally, רבי ירמיה explains that רבי חנינא's case is meat made impure through liquids. רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי disagree about whether such liquids pass on impurity by Torah law, and the ברייתא that proves this begins on the next amud.

steps.title: בית שמאי and בית הלל on burning פיגול, נותר and impure meat together
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: בית שמאי say פיגול, נותר and impure meat may not be burned together, and בית הלל say they may.
steps.simpleTranslation: פיגול, נותר, and impure meat: בית שמאי say they are not burned together. בית הלל say they are burned together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא it was in the middle of citing. The ברייתא now brings a related argument between בית שמאי and בית הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three kinds of meat are forbidden and must be burned. פיגול and נותר are only impure מדרבנן, while the impure meat is impure מן התורה, so burning them together would give the lighter items more impurity. בית שמאי forbid this, while בית הלל allow it, since everything is about to be burned anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: A קרבן ruined by the wrong intention (planning to eat or offer it after its proper time)
Meat of a קרבן left over after its time to be eaten has passed
Ritually impure
Burned together

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the same basic question that runs through the whole סוגיא: may you add impurity to something that is going to be destroyed anyway?

phrases.english: Piggul, notar, and impure meat:
Beit Shammai say:
They are not burned together.
And Beit Hillel say:
They are burned together.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַפִּיגּוּל וְהַנּוֹתָר וְהַטָּמֵא בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quotation begun on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: פיגול, נותר and impure meat are not burned together. בית הלל: they may be burned together.

steps.title: Why would רבי יוסי answer about רבי חנינא?
steps.stepSummary: If רבי מאיר learned his rule from רבי יהושע, why does רבי יוסי's reply seem to deal with רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you think רבי מאיר is speaking from the words of רבי יהושע, why does רבי יוסי answer him from the words of רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the argument between רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי in the משנה. It points out that the reply does not seem to match the claim.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The working assumption has been that רבי מאיר's source was רבי יהושע. But רבי יוסי's answer, 'that is not the comparison,' seems aimed at רבי חנינא's case. A reply should address the source the speaker actually used, so the גמרא is bothered by the mismatch.

keyTerms.meaning: If it enters your mind (if you assume)
Answers him back
The deputy כהן גדול

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר מִדִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ קָאָמַר,
phrases.english: that Rabbi Meir is speaking from the words of Rabbi Yehoshua,
why does Rabbi Yosei answer him
from the words of Rabbi Chanina the deputy High Priest?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the ברייתא and returns to the main discussion of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that רבי מאיר's source was רבי יהושע.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוסי's reply addresses רבי חנינא, so it seems רבי מאיר must have been quoting רבי חנינא.

steps.title: רב נחמן: רבי יוסי first misunderstood רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן explains that רבי יוסי thought רבי מאיר was quoting רבי חנינא, and רבי מאיר then corrected him: 'I mean רבי יהושע.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to him: רבי יוסי did not grasp רבי מאיר's point. He thought רבי מאיר was quoting רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים, so he answered that. Then רבי מאיר said to him: 'I am speaking from רבי יהושע.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers the question by describing the argument as a back-and-forth with more than one round. He starts the reconstruction here, and it continues in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי's first answer was aimed at רבי חנינא only because he misunderstood which source רבי מאיר meant. רבי מאיר then made clear that his source was רבי יהושע. So the assumption that רבי מאיר relied on רבי יהושע still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: He did not have it in mind (he did not grasp the point)
Thought or assumed
I am saying

steps.confusionAlert: Two different people say 'אמר ליה' in this passage. In the first round, רבי יוסי answers based on his mistake. In the next round, רבי מאיר is the one saying 'I mean רבי יהושע.' Keep track of who is speaking.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said to him:
Rabbi Yosei did not grasp his point,
for he thought that Rabbi Meir

phrases.aramaic: מִדְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא סְגַן הַכֹּהֲנִים קָאָמַר לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: was speaking to him from Rabbi Chanina the deputy High Priest,
and (Rabbi Meir) said to him:
phrases.notes: רבי מאיר clarifies what he meant.

phrases.english: I am speaking from Rabbi Yehoshua,

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן רַבִּי יוֹסֵי לָאו אַדַּעְתֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reconstructs the debate as having several rounds, with a misunderstanding at the start.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי's reply shows that רבי מאיר relied on רבי חנינא.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוסי's first reply came from his misunderstanding. רבי מאיר really relied on רבי יהושע.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's second answer: רבי יהושע does not help either
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי answers that even רבי יהושע's view gives no proof, because רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע agree that pure and impure are each burned separately.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי said to him: Even according to רבי יהושע, that is not the comparison. After all, רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע agree that you burn this one by itself and that one by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes רב נחמן's reconstruction. It is רבי יוסי's reply to רבי מאיר's clarification.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי now deals with רבי יהושע's view directly. He points to the agreed case in the משנה: when one item is pure and the other impure, both תנאים burn them separately. So רבי יהושע allowing burning together in a different case cannot prove that pure and impure תרומה may be burned together on ערב פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: That is not the comparison (the reasoning does not carry over)
Agrees
By itself

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב נחמן, the argument had two rounds. In round one, רבי יוסי rejected רבי חנינא as a source. In round two, רבי יוסי rejected רבי יהושע as a source, because of the case where everyone agrees to burn separately.

phrases.english: And (Rabbi Yosei) said to him:
Even according to Rabbi Yehoshua as well
that is not the comparison,

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָא מוֹדֶה רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
phrases.english: for Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua agree
that one burns this one by itself
and that one by itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲפִילּוּ לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ נָמֵי אֵינָהּ הִיא הַמִּדָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues and completes רב נחמן's reconstruction from step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Second stage of the reconstruction: רבי יוסי's actual reply to רבי מאיר's real source.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Once רבי מאיר names רבי יהושע, his proof should stand.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוסי rejects רבי יהושע as a source too, based on the agreed case of separate burning.

steps.title: But the comparison to רבי יהושע seems valid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יוסי says the comparison fails. It looks like a perfectly good comparison.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why is it 'not the comparison'? It is a fully valid comparison!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוסי's second answer from step 4. It sets up the discussion that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case where רבי יהושע allows burning together seems to work just like ערב פסח. In both cases, something not yet impure is about to be destroyed anyway, so making it impure causes no real loss. The גמרא therefore asks why רבי יוסי rejects a comparison that seems to fit exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: But why?
It is a fully valid comparison

phrases.english: But why is it not the comparison?
It is a fully valid comparison!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יוסי's reasoning as reconstructed in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's claim that רבי יהושע's view cannot be compared to burning on ערב פסח.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both cases share the same logic: making something impure is allowed when it is about to be destroyed anyway. So the comparison should hold.

steps.title: The barrel case is different because ordinary produce would be lost
steps.stepSummary: The comparison to רבי יהושע fails because in his case making the תרומה impure saves a large amount of חולין from being ruined.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because there is a loss of non-sacred produce.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 5. It explains why רבי יוסי said that רבי יהושע's case is no proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי יהושע's case, wine of תרומה is about to spill into a vat of impure חולין below. If it falls in, all that חולין becomes forbidden to non-כהנים, so רבי יהושע allows the תרומה to be made impure to prevent that big loss. Burning חמץ on ערב פסח causes no such loss, so there is no reason to allow burning the pure and impure together.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there; the case being compared is not the same
A loss (of money or property)
Ordinary, non-sacred produce

steps.confusionAlert: 'There' (הָתָם) refers to רבי יהושע's barrel case, not to the משנה about burning חמץ.

phrases.english: It is different there,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the broken barrel case of רבי יהושע.

phrases.english: because there is a loss of non-sacred produce.
phrases.notes: Without action, the impure חולין below would become forbidden mixed תרומה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers step 5's question of why the comparison fails.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהושע's permission to make תרומה impure seemed to apply to burning חמץ too.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהושע allowed it only to prevent a loss of חולין. Burning חמץ involves no such loss.

steps.title: רב ירמיה: the משנה's case also involves a loss of wood
steps.stepSummary: רב ירמיה objects that burning separately also causes a loss, because extra firewood is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ירמיה challenged this: In our משנה too there is a loss, a loss of wood!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ירמיה attacks the answer from step 6. He argues that the חמץ case also involves a loss.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the pure and impure תרומה must be burned separately, a second fire is needed, and that uses more wood. So the claim that 'there is no loss here' seems wrong, and the distinction from step 6 seems to collapse.

keyTerms.meaning: He strongly challenged it
Wood, firewood
Also, too

phrases.english: Rav Yirmeya strongly objected to it:
In our Mishnah too there is a loss of wood!
phrases.notes: Burning separately means building a second fire.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the distinction made in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 6 that the חמץ case involves no loss.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Separate burning needs extra wood, which is also a loss. So the two cases look alike after all.

steps.title: An elder answers: only a large loss counts
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים took a large loss into account, but not a small loss like some extra wood.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain elder said to him: For a great loss, they were concerned. For a small loss, they were not concerned.
steps.whatsHappening: An unnamed elder answers רב ירמיה's challenge. He explains that the size of the loss matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Losing a whole vat of חולין is a big loss, so it can justify making תרומה impure. A few pieces of wood are a small loss and do not justify it. The distinction from step 6 therefore stands.

keyTerms.meaning: A certain elder (an unnamed wise old man)
A large loss
A small loss
They (the חכמים) were concerned about

steps.whatToRemember: The distinction that defends רבי יוסי still stands. In רבי יהושע's barrel case, making תרומה impure was allowed to prevent a large loss. Saving a little wood is not enough of a reason.

phrases.english: A certain elder said to him:
About a great loss, they were concerned;
about a small loss, they were not concerned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב ירמיה's challenge and restores the distinction from step 6.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any loss, even of wood, would count.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a large loss, like ruined חולין, is taken into account. A little wood is not.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the dispute is only in the sixth hour
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן limits the argument between רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי to the sixth hour. In the seventh hour everyone agrees they may be burned together.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: The dispute is in the sixth hour, but in the seventh hour everyone agrees that we burn them together.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement opens a new topic: exactly when do רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי argue? רבי יוחנן says they argue only during the sixth hour of ערב פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the sixth hour, חמץ is forbidden only by the חכמים (דרבנן). There, רבי יוסי says the pure תרומה should not be made impure for a rabbinic rule. In the seventh hour, חמץ is forbidden by the תורה (דאורייתא), so everyone agrees that pure and impure חמץ of תרומה may be burned together.

keyTerms.meaning: A dispute, an argument between חכמים
In the sixth hour (when חמץ is forbidden only by rabbinic law)
In the seventh hour (when חמץ is forbidden by Torah law)
Everyone agrees

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the rule that the argument depends on whether the prohibition is rabbinic or from the תורה. The next step builds on that idea.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Asi said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
The dispute is in the sixth hour,
phrases.notes: The dispute is between רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: but in the seventh hour, all agree that we burn them together.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new question: the time frame of the dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute is only in the sixth hour (rabbinic חמץ). In the seventh hour (Torah-level חמץ), all agree that pure and impure תרומה may be burned together.

steps.title: רבי זירא suggests how רבי יוחנן reads the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא suggests that רבי יוחנן reads רבי חנינא's case as a Torah-level primary impurity together with a rabbinic secondary impurity. On this reading, רבי מאיר learned his rule from רבי חנינא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to רבי אסי: Shall we say that רבי יוחנן holds that the משנה speaks of a primary source of impurity from the Torah and a secondary impurity that is only rabbinic? And what does 'from their words' mean? From the words of רבי חנינא the deputy High Priest.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא proposes a conclusion that seems to follow from רבי יוחנן's statement. He asks רבי אסי whether this is really what רבי יוחנן means, which sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the dispute applies only to rabbinic חמץ, then רבי מאיר must have learned his rule from a case where something only rabbinically impure is made more impure. That fits רבי חנינא's case if the lighter impurity there is rabbinic. So 'from their words' would mean רבי חנינא, not רבי יהושע, which differs from רב נחמן's explanation in step 3.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (introduces a proposed inference)
He holds, he is of the opinion
A primary source of impurity
A secondary (derived) impurity
'From their words' (רבי מאיר's phrase in the משנה)
The deputy High Priest

steps.confusionAlert: 'Rabbinic' here describes the secondary impurity in רבי חנינא's case. It matches the rabbinic prohibition of חמץ in the sixth hour, and that match is the whole point of רבי זירא's suggestion.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא לְרַבִּי אַסִּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said to Rabbi Asi:
Shall we say that Rabbi Yochanan holds
that the Mishnah speaks of a primary source of impurity by Torah law
phrases.notes: This is רבי חנינא's case in the משנה.

phrases.english: and a secondary impurity by rabbinic law,
and what does 'from their words' mean?
From the words of Rabbi Chanina, the deputy High Priest.
phrases.notes: So רבי מאיר learned his rule from רבי חנינא, not from רבי יהושע.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from רבי יוחנן's statement in step 9 about how he reads the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבי יוחנן's limit to the sixth hour mean he reads רבי חנינא's case as involving a rabbinic secondary impurity, and that רבי מאיר learned his rule from רבי חנינא?

steps.title: רבי אסי says yes
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי confirms that רבי זירא understood רבי יוחנן correctly.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Yes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אסי answers רבי זירא's question with one word: yes. רבי יוחנן really does read the משנה that way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 10, רבי זירא asked whether רבי יוחנן reads רבי חנינא's case as a Torah-level primary impurity together with a rabbinic secondary impurity. רבי אסי confirms this reading. So, according to רבי יוחנן, רבי מאיר built his rule on רבי חנינא.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes (Aramaic)

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes.
phrases.notes: רבי אסי is answering רבי זירא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in Step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, רבי יוחנן reads the משנה as a Torah-level אב הטומאה together with a rabbinic ולד הטומאה, based on רבי חנינא.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's statement quoted directly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רבי יוחנן explicitly said this. The משנה deals with a Torah-level primary impurity and a rabbinic secondary impurity. "From their words" means from רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים. The dispute is only in the sixth hour.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated: רבי יוחנן said: Our משנה is about a Torah-level primary source of impurity and a rabbinic-level secondary impurity. What does "from their words" mean? From the words of רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים. The argument is in the sixth hour, but in the seventh hour everyone agrees they burn them together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רבי אסי's "yes" by quoting רבי יוחנן's own words. Both parts are now confirmed: the reading of רבי חנינא, and the sixth-hour limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "איתמר נמי" means this does not depend only on רבי אסי's report, because רבי יוחנן's statement exists in his own words. The word "מדבריהם" in the משנה is explained as pointing to רבי חנינא, which is where רבי מאיר learned his rule. The limit is restated as well. In the sixth hour חמץ is only rabbinically forbidden, so they argue. In the seventh hour it is forbidden by the Torah, so all agree.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated (an explicit quote that confirms the point)
A primary source of impurity
Something made impure by a primary source, which is a weaker level
"From their words", the phrase in the משנה being explained
The deputy כהן גדול

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן, רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי argue only in the sixth hour, when חמץ is rabbinically forbidden. In the seventh hour, when it is Torah-forbidden, everyone agrees pure and impure תרומה may be burned together.

phrases.english: It was also stated: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Our mishna is about a primary source of impurity by Torah law
and a secondary impurity by rabbinic law,
and what is "from their words"?
phrases.notes: This explains the word used in the משנה.

phrases.english: From the words of Rabbi Chanina, the deputy High Priest.
And the dispute is in the sixth hour,
but in the seventh, all agree one burns them together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms Step 11 with רבי יוחנן's explicit statement.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוחנן reads the משנה as based on רבי חנינא and limits the dispute to the sixth hour.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A direct quote of רבי יוחנן (איתמר).

steps.title: Possible support from פיגול, נותר and impure meat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to prove רבי יוחנן's seventh-hour rule from a ברייתא. There, בית הלל allow burning פיגול, נותר and impure meat together, even though all of them are forbidden by the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this supports him? פיגול, נותר and impure sacrificial meat: בית שמאי say they are not burned together, and בית הלל say they are burned together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a ברייתא that might support רבי יוחנן's claim that everyone, even רבי יוסי, agrees in the seventh hour.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פיגול, נותר and impure meat are all forbidden by the Torah. בית הלל let them be burned together, and רבי יוסי surely follows בית הלל. The suggested point is that when items are Torah-forbidden, there is no concern about burning them together. That would match חמץ in the seventh hour.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say this supports him?
A קרבן made invalid by an improper intention about when it would be eaten
Meat of a קרבן left over past its time
Burned together

phrases.english: Shall we say this supports him:
Piggul, notar, and impure sacrificial meat,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: אֵין נִשְׂרָפִין כְּאַחַת,
phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: they are not burned together,
and Beit Hillel say: they are burned together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to bring outside support for the seventh-hour rule stated in Step 12.
steps.raayaObject: That even רבי יוסי allows burning together items that are forbidden by the Torah, as with חמץ in the seventh hour.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about פיגול, נותר and impure meat, where בית הלל allow burning them together.

steps.title: Rejected: פיגול and נותר are already rabbinically impure
steps.stepSummary: The proof fails. פיגול and נותר already carry rabbinic impurity, since they make the hands impure. So burning them with impure meat does not really add impurity to something pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because they have impurity by rabbinic law. As we learned: פיגול and נותר make the hands impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof from Step 13. The case of פיגול and נותר is different from pure חמץ of תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פיגול and נותר are already impure on a rabbinic level, so burning them with impure meat is not making something clean impure. Pure חמץ of תרומה in the seventh hour is forbidden but has no impurity at all. So רבי יוסי could still object to burning it with impure תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there
They make the hands impure (a rabbinic decree)

steps.confusionAlert: The proof does not fail because פיגול is less forbidden. It fails because פיגול is already impure, while pure חמץ of תרומה is not.

phrases.english: It is different there:
since they have impurity by rabbinic law.
As we learned: piggul and notar
render the hands impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in Step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only this proof. רבי יוחנן's rule itself is not disproven.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: פיגול and נותר are already rabbinically impure, unlike pure חמץ of תרומה, so the cases are not alike.

steps.title: Second possible support: moldy bread
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries another proof. Moldy bread that only a dog can eat still counts as food for impurity, yet it is burned together with impure תרומה on פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this supports him? Bread that got moldy and became unfit for people to eat, but a dog can eat it, can become impure with the impurity of food if it is the size of an egg. And it is burned with impure תרומה on פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא that might support רבי יוחנן. This step sets up the proof, and the next step responds to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The moldy bread is still food, so it can become impure. Even so, it may be burned together with impure תרומה, because it has lost its value as human food. This ruling would follow רבי יוסי, since רבי מאיר allows burning together even fresh bread. The suggestion is that רבי יוסי allows it here, so he should also allow it for חמץ in the seventh hour, which is forbidden by the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: Became moldy
The impurity that applies to food
The size of an egg, the minimum amount for food impurity
It is burned together with the impure תרומה

phrases.english: Shall we say this supports him:
Bread that became moldy
and became unfit for a person to eat,
but a dog can eat it,
it becomes impure with food impurity at an egg-bulk,
and it is burned with the impure on Passover.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected in Step 14, the גמרא tries a new source to support Step 12.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוסי allows burning pure and impure together when the pure item has lost its value, which would also fit Torah-forbidden חמץ in the seventh hour.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about moldy bread that only a dog can eat.

steps.title: Moldy bread is just dust
steps.stepSummary: The proof from moldy bread fails, because bread that only a dog can eat is treated like dust, not food.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because it is just plain dust.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from step 15. Moldy bread that people cannot eat is treated as worthless dust, so making it impure causes no real loss.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא admits the moldy bread can still become impure as food, since a dog can eat it. But for people it is worthless, like dust, so making it impure causes no real loss. That is why even רבי יוסי allows burning it with impure תרומה. It proves nothing about real, edible pure חמץ of תרומה in the seventh hour.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there; the case you brought is not comparable
Mere dust; something with no legal value

phrases.english: It is different there,
phrases.notes: In the case of the moldy bread from step 15.

phrases.english: because it is just plain dust.
phrases.notes: It can still become impure, but it is worthless to people, so nothing is lost by making it impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from moldy bread
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only this proof; רבי יוחנן's rule still stands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The moldy bread is worthless to people, like dust, so making it impure causes no loss. That is unlike edible pure תרומה.

steps.title: Why mention that they concede?
steps.stepSummary: Suppose רבי מאיר learns from רבי חנינא. Then why does רבי יוסי bring up what רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע agree on?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is the point of 'he concedes'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רבי יוחנן's reading, where רבי מאיר learns from רבי חנינא. It asks why רבי יוסי then mentions the concession of רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יוסי answers רבי מאיר by saying that רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע agree about a certain case. But רבי מאיר's proof came from רבי חנינא, not from them. So it seems their agreement has nothing to do with the argument.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if your explanation is correct
Concedes; agrees

phrases.english: If so,
phrases.notes: If רבי מאיר's source is רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים.

phrases.english: what is the point of 'he concedes'?
phrases.notes: Refers to רבי יוסי's statement in the משנה about what רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע agree on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רבי יוחנן's reading of the משנה from step 12 and challenges it
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's reading that רבי מאיר learned from רבי חנינא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the proof comes from רבי חנינא, then רבי יוסי's mention of רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע seems beside the point.

steps.title: Even רבי יהושע would not allow pure with impure
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי means that even lenient רבי יהושע only allows burning doubtful תרומה with impure, not pure with impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what רבי יוסי is saying to רבי מאיר: even according to רבי יהושע, who is lenient, his leniency is about burning doubtful תרומה with impure תרומה. But pure with impure, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי יוסי mentions רבי יהושע. He is showing that even the most lenient opinion does not go as far as רבי מאיר does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע allows burning תרומה תלויה, whose purity is in doubt, together with impure תרומה. רבי יוסי argues that this is the limit of the leniency. Burning definitely pure תרומה with impure תרומה is a bigger step, and even רבי יהושע never allowed it.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means
Rules leniently
In doubt; תרומה whose purity is uncertain

phrases.english: This is what he is saying to him:
Rabbi Yosei to Rabbi Meir:
Even according to Rabbi Yehoshua, who is lenient,
when he is lenient, it is with doubtful and impure,
phrases.notes: Burning doubtful תרומה together with impure תרומה.

phrases.english: but with pure and impure, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the purpose of a statement in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The mention of רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע seemed to have nothing to do with רבי חנינא's case.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוסי uses רבי יהושע to show that even the most lenient view stops short of burning pure תרומה with impure.

steps.title: But the comparison seems to work
steps.stepSummary: If רבי מאיר learns from רבי חנינא, why does רבי יוסי say the comparison fails? It looks like a good comparison.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why is it 'not the right comparison'? It is a perfectly good comparison!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוסי's words 'אינה היא המדה'. Using רבי יוחנן's reading, רבי מאיר's comparison seems correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא's case puts rabbinic-level impure meat together with Torah-level impure meat. Pure תרומה in the sixth hour is forbidden only by rabbinic law. So the two cases seem to match, and it is unclear why רבי יוסי rejects the comparison.

keyTerms.meaning: A measure or comparison; a fair way to learn one case from another
That is not the right comparison (רבי יוסי's words in the משנה)

phrases.english: If so,
phrases.notes: If רבי מאיר learns from רבי חנינא.

phrases.english: why is it 'not the right comparison'?
phrases.notes: Quoting רבי יוסי in the משנה.

phrases.english: It is a perfectly good comparison!
phrases.notes: In both cases, something impure only by rabbinic law goes together with something impure by Torah law.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, אַמַּאי אֵינָהּ הִיא הַמִּדָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to רבי יוחנן's reading, aimed at a different phrase of רבי יוסי
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's statement 'אינה היא המדה' under רבי יוחנן's reading
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both cases involve something that is only rabbinically problematic being burned with something impure by Torah law. So the comparison should work.

steps.title: Meat made impure through liquids
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה explains that רבי חנינא's case is meat made impure by liquids that touched a שרץ. רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי each follow their own view about that impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: Here we are dealing with meat that became impure through liquids that became impure from a שרץ. רבי מאיר follows his own reasoning, and רבי יוסי follows his own reasoning.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה answers the challenge by saying exactly which case of רבי חנינא is meant. The disagreement over the comparison comes from an older disagreement between רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The meat in רבי חנינא's case got its impurity from liquids, not directly from the שרץ. רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי disagree about whether liquids make other things impure by Torah law or only by rabbinic law. If it is rabbinic, the meat is pure by Torah law, so it compares well to pure תרומה (רבי מאיר). If it is Torah law, the meat is truly impure, so it does not compare (רבי יוסי). The גמרא will go on to show where each one holds this.

keyTerms.meaning: Liquids, which can pass on impurity
A creeping animal; a primary source of impurity (אב הטומאה)
Follows his own reasoning from elsewhere

steps.whatToRemember: The argument about burning pure תרומה with impure depends on another argument: whether liquids make other things impure by Torah law or by rabbinic law.
steps.confusionAlert: The meat did not touch the שרץ directly. The liquids touched the שרץ, and then the meat touched the liquids. That middle step is the key to the whole answer.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:
Here it is about meat that became impure
phrases.notes: The meat in רבי חנינא's case.

phrases.english: through liquids that became impure because of a creeping animal,
and רבי מאיר follows his own reasoning,
and רבי יוסי follows his own reasoning.
phrases.notes: Their known disagreement about the strength of impurity from liquids.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: הָכָא בְּבָשָׂר שֶׁנִּטְמָא בְּמַשְׁקִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the case more exactly and linking it to an existing dispute
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי חנינא's case seemed to match pure תרומה exactly, so רבי יוסי's rejection made no sense.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is meat made impure through liquids. Whether the comparison works depends on each תנא's view of how strong impurity from liquids is.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: impure liquids pass on impurity only by rabbinic law
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר holds that liquids pass on impurity to other things only מדרבנן. So the meat in רבי חנינא's case is pure by Torah law, and the case really is pure with impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר follows his own view. He said that the impurity of liquids, when it comes to making other things impure, is only rabbinic.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the first half of רבי ירמיה's answer. It explains why רבי מאיר is able to learn from רבי חנינא's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי חנינא's case, the meat became impure only through liquids that had touched a שרץ. For רבי מאיר, liquids pass on impurity only מדרבנן, so by Torah law the meat is completely pure. Burning it together with impure meat is therefore really burning pure with impure. That is why רבי מאיר compares it to burning pure and impure תרומה together on ערב פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning (a view he holds elsewhere)
Impurity of liquids
To make other things impure
By rabbinic law (not from the Torah)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי מאיר is not saying the liquids themselves are pure. He is only saying that their power to make *other* things impure, like the meat, is rabbinic. So the meat is pure only by Torah law.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir follows his own reasoning,
for he said: the impurity of liquids
to make others impure is rabbinic.
phrases.notes: So meat touched by such liquid is pure by Torah law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the רבי מאיר half of רבי ירמיה's answer from Step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The two תנאים follow different underlying views (לטעמיה).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed that רבי חנינא's case is simply a good comparison, so רבי יוסי should not have rejected it.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי מאיר, the meat is pure by Torah law, so the case is truly pure with impure and the comparison works.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: impure liquids pass on impurity by Torah law
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי holds that liquids pass on impurity מדאורייתא. So the meat is truly impure and the case is only impure with impure. The גמרא then opens a ברייתא as the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי follows his own view. He said that the impurity of liquids, when it comes to making other things impure, is from the Torah. As it was taught in a ברייתא:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second half of רבי ירמיה's answer, explaining why רבי יוסי rejects the comparison. The last word, "דתניא", is a setup line that opens a ברייתא coming next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוסי, the liquids really do make the meat impure by Torah law. So רבי חנינא's case is burning impure meat with more impure meat, just at different levels. That cannot prove we may burn pure תרומה with impure תרומה, so the comparison fails.

keyTerms.meaning: By Torah law

steps.whatToRemember: The whole argument between רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי about רבי חנינא's case depends on one question: do liquids pass on impurity to other things by rabbinic law (רבי מאיר) or by Torah law (רבי יוסי)?
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains רבי יוסי's statement that the comparison fails. It is not a weak reading of רבי חנינא. It comes from a basic disagreement about how impurity works, and the ברייתא that follows will show it.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei follows his own reasoning,
for he said: the impurity of liquids
to make others impure is from the Torah.
phrases.notes: So the meat is impure by Torah law.

phrases.english: As it was taught:
phrases.notes: Opens the ברייתא that is the source for these views.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the רבי יוסי half that balances Step 21, then introduces a supporting ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The two תנאים follow different underlying views (לטעמיה).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי חנינא's case looked like a fine comparison, so it was unclear why רבי יוסי rejected it.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי יוסי, the meat is impure by Torah law, so the case is only impure with impure and proves nothing about pure with impure.
